title: Builder Signals · 2026-07-29
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 29 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 11 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex & ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI's Codex & ChatGPT lead Thibault Sottiaux spent the week celebrating ChatGPT Work's rapid adoption—announcing usage-limit resets for all paid Codex/ChatGPT Work users, then joking that he felt "like a limit reset" himself and was stepping away from X to recharge. Low on substance individually, but the signal is clear: OpenAI is pushing hard on the enterprise side, and the product team is visibly in high-energy crunch mode. A moment worth noting for anyone tracking OpenAI's enterprise play.
featured.insightZh: OpenAI Codex 和 ChatGPT 的负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 这周连发几条庆祝 ChatGPT Work 的快速起量——他宣布给所有付费用户重置了 Codex 和 ChatGPT Work 的额度限制，还半开玩笑地说自己"感觉像被重置了一样"、要暂时离开 X 充个电。这几条帖子本身信息量不大，但胜在信号明确：OpenAI 在企业侧（ChatGPT Work）的推进节奏很猛，产品团队处在明显的兴奋和加班状态。对关注 OpenAI 企业级布局的人来说，这是一个值得记下来的时间点。

featured.title: Peter Yang · 实用 AI 教程与访谈创作者
featured.summaryEn: AI-tutorials creator Peter Yang shared a vivid example of what "agent-era work" actually looks like: OpenAI DevEx's Jason was on a bike ride when a coworker asked him to fix a launch video. He remotely connected to Codex from his phone, had it use computer-use to edit, export, and post the video back to Slack—then told Codex to "check the thread every 30 minutes for feedback and export V2, V3, V4." By the time he got home, the video was greenlit. Not a demo, a real workflow: agents can now handle iterate-on-feedba…
featured.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 分享了一个很能说明"agent 时代工作方式"的真实案例：OpenAI DevEx 的 Jason 骑行途中被同事要求改一个发布视频，他直接用手机远程连上 Codex，让它用 computer use 编辑视频、导出、发回 Slack；然后甚至给 Codex 下了个持续指令——"每 30 分钟检查一次 thread 里的反馈，导出 V2、V3、V4"。等他骑车到家，发布视频已经被批准了。这不是演示，是真实工作流：agent 已经能承担"根据反馈反复迭代 + 主动查收消息"这种典型人类协作动作。

featured.title: Granola 创始人谈"第一波 AI 应用之后是什么"
featured.summaryEn: Meeting notes were never the endgame—the real opportunity is reinventing the interface for how humans and AI work together. And once an agent is good enough to build any software, it's great at any knowledge work, which is splitting work into two surfaces: async delegation in Slack, and deep work in Codex/Claude-style apps where you and the agent sit in the same place. In this AI & I episode, Every CEO Dan Shipper talks with Chris, cofounder/CEO of Granola (the $1.5B AI meeting app), about how startups survive in the AI era. Chris's first counterintuitive point is about competition: Notion, OpenAI, and Zoom all copied Granola's meeting notes, but it affected him far less than expected—because he's convinced meeting notes aren't the endgame; the real prize is "what interface we use to work and how we work in an AI-native world." So he isn't anxious about being copied, since everyone is s…
featured.insightZh: 会议记录从来不是终点——真正的机会是重新发明"人和 AI 一起工作"的界面；而当 agent 好到能构建任何软件时，它就能胜任任何知识工作，这正在把工作切成两个面：Slack 里的异步委派协作、以及 Codex/Claude 这类"你和 agent 坐在同一个 app 里"的深度工作面。 在这期 AI & I 里，Every CEO Dan Shipper 和 Granola（估值 15 亿美元的 AI 会议应用）创始人兼 CEO Chris 聊了创业公司在 AI 时代如何自处。Chris 的第一个反直觉观点是关于竞争：Notion、OpenAI、Zoom 都抄了 Granola 的会议记录，但对他影响远比想象中小——因为他坚信会议记录不是终局，真正的机会是"在 AI 原生世界里我们用什么界面工作、怎么工作"。所以他不焦虑别人抄，因为大家都还在这场计算革命的极早期。 Dan 则贡献了本期最锋利的实操洞察：工作正在分叉成两个面。一个是 Slack 里的异步委派——多人、协作、有时主动的工作（比如 Slack bot 每天早上汇报修了哪些 bug、推了哪些 PR，你可以直接让它去起一个 PR）；因为大多数 AI 现在还是单人的，你就在公开频道里和它协作。另一个面是 Codex/Claude 桌面 app 这种"你和 agent 坐在同一个地方"的深度工作面。Dan 说他几乎所有时间都花在 Codex 里，甚至把邮件、换宽带这种事都丢给它——让 Codex 在 in-app 浏览器里登录 Verizon 网站、和客服聊天，直到把宽带套餐换好，还帮他算清楚有没有隐藏费用。 两人共同的战略结论很值得咨询/产品人记下来：Chris 认为软件公司在 AI 时代的角色是"骨架"——AI 是灵活的肌肉和韧带，但只有在软件给出的正确结构和上下文里才能发挥。所以 Granola 的策略是：在一切与会议相关的事上做到全球最好，并成为"捕获上下文、给任何 agent 供能"的最佳方式（API/MCP 会大幅加强）。Dan 补充了那个经典画面——Hugging Face 一位创始人花几个月在 C…

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie pushed back on the popular "AI will destroy jobs" narrative with front-line evidence: the enterprises he talks to across industries are still hiring—just with a shift in the kinds of roles. He sees Jevons paradox playing out for real: AI lets companies do more, so they hire engineers to tackle problems they couldn't before, hire in sales to go deeper on client relationships, and hire internal FDEs to deploy AI. His sharp bottom line: anyone using AI merely to cut costs eventually gets outcompet…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 对"AI 会毁灭就业"的流行叙事泼了盆冷水，而且他的论据来自一线：他接触的大量各行业企业其实还在招人，只是招聘的岗位结构在变。他观察到 Jevons 悖论正在真实上演——AI 让企业能做更多事，于是他们招工程师去攻以前搞不定的难题、招销售因为现在能更深地经营客户关系、招内部 FDE 去部署 AI。他的核心判断很锋利：只把 AI 用来砍成本的公司，最终会被那些用 AI 更好服务客户、驱动业务突破的公司竞争淘汰。

items.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人）
items.summaryEn: Ex-Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana lead, now Meta AI Sr Director, Madhu Guru offered a sharp diagnosis of why product reviews feel annoying: the best reviews compress months of learning into an hour by simulating the market's reaction to your ideas. But that only works when the people in the room deeply understand the space, have great product sense, strong opinions, and are often right. Too many reviews have drifted toward status updates, leadership visibility, and cross-functional alignment—so people resent them,…
items.insightZh: 前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人、现 Meta AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru 对"产品评审会为什么让人烦"下了个精准诊断：最好的产品评审能把几个月的学习压缩进一小时——靠的是在会议室里模拟市场对你想法的反应。但这只在与会者深刻理解领域、有强产品直觉、有鲜明观点且往往判断正确时才成立。太多评审会已经滑向了状态汇报、给领导刷存在感、跨部门对齐，于是自然让人反感，因为它变成了 overhead 而非学习。对任何管团队、开评审会的人，这是个值得贴在墙上的标准。

items.title: swyx · Latent Space / Smol AI / AI Engineer 创办人
items.summaryEn: swyx dropped two sharp takes this week. First: dollar-cost per input/output token "died as a relevant cost measure sometime last year"—if you haven't switched your x-axis to $/task, he argues you can barely be taken seriously now. Second, a harder self-critique: as the originator of the "agent lab thesis" (getting the evals/routing/interactivity/ROI focus right), he admits the biggest argument against himself is that Claude Code got "accidentally open-sourced" this year and approximately nothing happened to it or…
items.insightZh: swyx 这周抛了两个尖锐观点。其一：把每输入/输出 token 的美元成本当作关键成本指标"去年某个时候就已经死了"——如果你还没把横轴换成 $/task（每任务成本），那在他看来现在已经很难被认真对待。其二自我批判更狠：作为"agent lab 论题"的提出者（把评测、路由、交互性、ROI 的重心押对了），他坦承对自己最大的反驳是——Claude Code 今年"意外地被开源"了，结果它自己和竞品的 roadmap 几乎都没受什么影响。这是难得的、创作者对自己核心论点的公开压力测试。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch shared two hard-nosed takes on agent security. First, model-layer: in their cybersecurity benchmarks, Grok 4.5 emerged as the best price-performance security model—10x cheaper than Sol, 5.7x cheaper than Opus 5, at near-frontier perf (Sol still leads). Second, more technical and more important for engineering teams: Kimi's paper underlines how critical the security boundary is for agents—container-level isolation isn't enough; in their experiments agents crashed the host via kernel panic…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 分享了两条关于 agent 安全的硬核观察。其一是模型层：在他们的网络安全基准里，Grok 4.5 成了性价比最优的安全 AI 模型——比 Sol 便宜 10 倍、比 Opus 5 便宜 5.7 倍，性能却接近第一梯队（Sol 仍是前沿）。其二更技术、也更值得工程团队注意：Kimi 的论文说明了 agent 运行环境的安全边界有多关键——容器级隔离不够，实验里 agent 甚至通过内核 panic 把宿主机搞崩了；而 Firecracker 微虚拟机（如 Vercel Sandbox）才是安全的。对任何要跑生产级 agent 的团队，这是直接的架构提醒。

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Linear's head of product Nan Yu punctured the logic behind a lot of today's "AI wrapper" products in one line: a lot of very smart people work very hard to make a product very good and nice to use; if you have very smart people, you should have them make *your own* product very good—and pay us a nominal fee to use ours. A pointed jab at the classic build-vs-buy call, especially aimed at engineering cultures that fetishize doing everything in-house.
items.insightZh: Linear 产品负责人 Nan Yu 一句话戳破了当下很多"AI 套壳产品"的逻辑漏洞：很多非常聪明的人非常努力地把产品做得很好用；如果你手上就有这些聪明人，那你应该让他们把你自己的产品做得很好用——然后付一笔象征性的费用来用我们的产品就好。这是对"聪明团队到底该自建还是该买"这个经典决策的一次犀利反讽，尤其适用于那些迷信"什么都自己做"的工程文化。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger ("ClawFather") had a post vividly showing where agent collaboration is heading: "My agent reported a bug, their agent fixed it—in the same night." (Referring to @jarredsumner's robobun setup, two agents closing a report-to-fix loop overnight.) Another vented on behalf of security teams: they do all the amazing security work with some of the world's best teams, and people still think they're unsafe. For anyone building agent infrastructure, one is an exciting slice of the future, the ot…
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger（"ClawFather"）这周有条帖子生动展示了 agent 协作的未来形态："我的 agent 报了个 bug，他们的 agent 当晚就修好了。"——指的是 @jarredsumner 的 robobun 配置，两个 agent 隔空一夜完成了报 bug 到修 bug 的闭环。另一条则替安全团队叫屈：他们和世界顶级团队一起做了大量安全工作，结果大家还是觉得他们不安全。对做 agent 基础设施的人，这两条一条是激动人心的未来切片，一条是"安全很难被感知"的现实吐槽。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad framed this AI wave grandly: we're entering a new era of exploration. Our ancestors mapped the Earth, then explored space; our generation may explore the "computational universe"—the vast space of algorithms, programs, proofs, and designs that AI agents can search. A vision-level, philosophical statement, but a useful mental model for understanding why companies like Replit are betting on agents' autonomous exploration capabilities.
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 给这一波 AI 浪潮下了个宏大的框架：我们正进入一个新的探索时代。祖先绘制了地球的地图，后来探索了太空；而我们这一代人也许要探索的是"计算宇宙"——那片由 AI agent 可以搜索的算法、程序、证明和设计构成的广阔空间。这是一句偏愿景、偏哲学的表态，但对理解 Replit 这类公司为什么押注 agent 自主探索能力，是个有用的心智模型。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari ran a practical experiment: for a full two-week trip he used Claude Code as his primary interface (booking, lookups, general logistics), then had it run a complete retrospective on the whole trip—summarizing what could be done better next time. Another data point for "using a coding agent for pure life/knowledge work," echoing this episode's core thesis from Dan Shipper: once an agent is good enough to build any software, it's also great at any knowledge work.
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 做了个很实用的实验：整整两周的旅行，他把 Claude Code 当作主要交互界面（订行程、查信息、处理各种事务），回来后又让它对整段旅程做了一次完整复盘——总结哪些地方下次能做得更好。这是"用编程 agent 处理纯生活/知识工作"的又一个数据点，呼应了本期 podcast 里 Dan Shipper 的核心观点：一旦 agent 好到能构建任何软件，它做任何知识工作也会很好。
